intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GRIN2D gene (602717) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GRIN2D gene.
checks.evidence_quote: GRIN2D Recurrent De Novo Dominant Mutation Causes a Severe Epileptic Encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The paper reports a heterozygous GRIN2D mutation as the cause of epileptic encephalopathy. The DEE46 label is OMIM's name for this disorder.

checks.claim: The GRIN2D gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene name the paper uses.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 is a severe neurologic disorder that begins in infancy or early childhood. Affected individuals have refractory seizures and global developmental delay with intellectual disability. The disorder is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in GRIN2D, which encodes the GluN2D subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor. Functional studies show that the mutations increase receptor function (gain of function).

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 is a severe neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Causes a Severe Epileptic Encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The title calls the disorder severe.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 begins in infancy or early childhood.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract says the patients are children but gives no age of onset. Onset in infancy or early childhood may be in the full text, but only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: Individuals with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 have refractory seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Because both individuals' seizures had proven refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications
checks.explanation: The abstract says both patients' seizures were refractory.

checks.claim: Individuals with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 have global developmental delay with intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: three unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions severe developmental delay but not intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in GRIN2D.
checks.evidence_quote: we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a de novo heterozygous GRIN2D mutation.

checks.claim: GRIN2D encodes the GluN2D subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: The resulting GluN2D p.Val667Ile exchange occurs in the M3 transmembrane domain
checks.explanation: The abstract names GluN2D as the NMDAR subunit encoded by GRIN2D.

checks.claim: Functional studies show that GRIN2D mutations causing developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 increase receptor function, a gain of function.
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold, increases channel open probability by 6-fold
checks.explanation: The functional studies show a gain of function.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) reported 2 unrelated children with an epileptic encephalopathy. Both had early-onset seizures that did not respond to treatment, and both had profound developmental delay. Each child carried the same de novo mutation in GRIN2D.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) reported 2 unrelated children with an epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract describes 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy.

checks.claim: Both children reported by Li et al. (2016) had early-onset seizures.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the age at seizure onset (abstract only).

checks.claim: The seizures of both children reported by Li et al. (2016) did not respond to treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: Because both individuals' seizures had proven refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications
checks.explanation: Both patients' seizures were refractory to standard treatment.

checks.claim: Both children reported by Li et al. (2016) had profound developmental delay.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe profound developmental delay; it only mentions improvement in development (abstract only).

checks.claim: Each of the 2 children reported by Li et al. (2016) carried the same de novo mutation in GRIN2D.
checks.evidence_quote: we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)
checks.explanation: The same recurrent de novo mutation was found in both children.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous GRIN2D mutations in the patients reported by Li et al. (2016) arose de novo, which fits autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The heterozygous GRIN2D mutations in the patients reported by Li et al. (2016) arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)
checks.explanation: The abstract states the heterozygous mutations arose de novo.

checks.claim: The de novo occurrence of heterozygous GRIN2D mutations in the patients reported by Li et al. (2016) is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: GRIN2D Recurrent De Novo Dominant Mutation
checks.explanation: The title calls the mutation dominant.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) used exome sequencing to study 2 unrelated patients with epileptic encephalopathy. Both carried the same de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GRIN2D gene, V667I. In functional studies, NMDA receptors containing the mutant subunit were more sensitive to the agonists glutamate and glycine, which indicated a gain of function. In vitro, the FDA-approved NMDA receptor channel blockers memantine and ketamine inhibited the mutant receptors. Li et al. (2016) treated the patients with these drugs and reported some reduction in seizures.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) used exome sequencing to study 2 unrelated patients with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract says both exome and candidate panel sequencing were used, not exome sequencing alone.

checks.claim: Both patients with epileptic encephalopathy studied by Li et al. (2016) carried the same de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GRIN2D gene, V667I.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D
checks.explanation: Both patients carried V667I; the draft's notation is equivalent.

checks.claim: In functional studies by Li et al. (2016), NMDA receptors containing the GRIN2D V667I mutant subunit were more sensitive to the agonists glutamate and glycine.
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold
checks.explanation: Higher agonist potency means greater sensitivity to glutamate and glycine.

checks.claim: The increased agonist sensitivity of NMDA receptors containing the GRIN2D V667I subunit indicated a gain of function.
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold, increases channel open probability by 6-fold
checks.explanation: The paper calls the mutation gain-of-function. That conclusion rests on several findings, including increased agonist potency.

checks.claim: In vitro, the FDA-approved NMDA receptor channel blockers memantine and ketamine inhibited NMDA receptors containing the GRIN2D V667I mutant subunit.
checks.evidence_quote: the sensitivity of mutant NMDARs to FDA-approved NMDAR antagonists was evaluated. Based on these results, oral memantine was administered
checks.explanation: The abstract says mutant receptors were tested against FDA-approved NMDAR antagonists. It does not say which drugs were tested in vitro, and it does not state that memantine and ketamine inhibited the mutant receptors.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) treated the 2 patients with the GRIN2D V667I mutation with memantine and ketamine.
checks.evidence_quote: oral memantine was administered to both children, with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus, with dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.
checks.explanation: Both children got memantine, but only the older proband got ketamine, together with magnesium.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) reported some reduction in seizures in the patients with the GRIN2D V667I mutation treated with NMDA receptor channel blockers.
checks.evidence_quote: oral memantine was administered to both children, with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development
checks.explanation: The abstract reports reduced seizure burden after treatment.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) based treatment on the gain-of-function mechanism and gave NMDA receptor channel blockers, including memantine and ketamine and/or magnesium. They reported that seizure control improved in their patients with GRIN2D mutations.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) based treatment of patients with GRIN2D mutations on the gain-of-function mechanism.
checks.evidence_quote: Based on these results, oral memantine was administered to both children
checks.explanation: Treatment was based on in vitro results showing the mutant receptors were sensitive to NMDAR antagonists. The abstract does not explicitly say it was based on the gain-of-function mechanism, though antagonist therapy for a gain-of-function mutation implies it.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) gave patients with GRIN2D mutations NMDA receptor channel blockers, including memantine and ketamine and/or magnesium.
checks.evidence_quote: oral memantine was administered to both children, with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus, with dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.
checks.explanation: The patients received memantine, and the older proband also received ketamine and magnesium.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) reported that seizure control improved in their patients with GRIN2D mutations treated with NMDA receptor channel blockers.
checks.evidence_quote: with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development
checks.explanation: The abstract reports improved seizure burden.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) found a de novo heterozygous val667-to-ile (V667I) mutation in the GRIN2D gene in 2 unrelated patients with epileptic encephalopathy. The mutation lies in the M3 transmembrane region of GluN2D. Functional studies of the mutant receptors showed a gain of function, including increased sensitivity to glutamate and glycine.

checks.claim: Li et al. (2016) found a de novo heterozygous val667-to-ile (V667I) mutation in the GRIN2D gene in 2 unrelated patients with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D, identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract reports this mutation in 2 unrelated patients.

checks.claim: The GRIN2D V667I mutation lies in the M3 transmembrane region of GluN2D.
checks.evidence_quote: The resulting GluN2D p.Val667Ile exchange occurs in the M3 transmembrane domain involved in channel gating.
checks.explanation: The abstract places V667I in the M3 transmembrane domain.

checks.claim: Functional studies of NMDA receptors carrying the GRIN2D V667I mutation showed a gain of function.
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold
checks.explanation: The functional studies show a gain of function.

checks.claim: NMDA receptors carrying the GRIN2D V667I mutation showed increased sensitivity to glutamate and glycine.
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold
checks.explanation: Higher potency of glutamate and glycine means increased sensitivity to them.
